messages.content:
You are an expert programmer working in a language based on lambda calculus.
Your goal is to write programs that accomplish the tasks specified by the user.
This is a domain-specific language for regular expressions that specify string transformations.

Write programs using the available functions:

'.' :: tsubstr

empty_string :: tsubstr

'a' :: tsubstr

'b' :: tsubstr

'c' :: tsubstr

'd' :: tsubstr

'e' :: tsubstr

regex_not :: tsubstr -> tsubstr

regex_or :: tsubstr -> tsubstr -> tsubstr

regex_concat :: tsubstr -> tsubstr -> tsubstr

regex_match :: tsubstr -> tsubstr -> bool

regex_split :: tsubstr -> tfullstr -> list(tsubstr)

regex_flatten :: list(tsubstr) -> tfullstr

regex_tail :: list(tsubstr) -> tsubstr

regex_append :: t0 -> list(t0) -> list(t0)

regex_reverse_cdr :: list(t0) -> list(t0)

regex_if :: bool -> t0 -> t0 -> t0

regex_cons :: t0 -> list(t0) -> list(t0)

regex_car :: list(t0) -> t0

regex_cdr :: list(t0) -> list(t0)

regex_map :: (t0 -> t1) -> list(t0) -> list(t1)

replace_if_match_split :: tfullstr -> tsubstr -> tsubstr -> tfullstr
(lambda (lambda (lambda (regex_flatten (regex_map (lambda (regex_if (regex_match $1 $0) $2 $0)) (regex_split '.' $2))))))
description: A function that replaces a substring in a full string based on a condition. It checks if the substring matches a pattern in the full string, and if it does, replaces it with another substring. It then splits the full string by a delimiter.

replace_substring_based_on_condition :: tfullstr -> (tsubstr -> tsubstr) -> tfullstr
(lambda (lambda (regex_flatten (regex_map $0 (regex_split '.' $1)))))
description: A function that replaces substrings in a full string based on a condition. It maps over the substrings split by '.' in the full string and applies a transformation function to each substring.

replace_first_letter_with_given_substring :: tfullstr -> tsubstr -> tfullstr
(lambda (lambda (regex_flatten (regex_cons $0 (regex_cdr (regex_split '.' $1))))))
description: A function that replaces the first letter of each word in a full string with a specified substring. It splits the full string by '.' and replaces the first character of each word with the given substring.

replace_substrings_based_on_function :: tfullstr -> (tsubstr -> tsubstr) -> tfullstr
(lambda (lambda (regex_flatten (regex_map $0 (regex_split empty_string $1)))))
description: A function that replaces substrings in a full string based on a provided transformation function. It splits the full string into substrings and applies the transformation function to each substring.

append_reversed_substrings_after_split :: tfullstr -> tsubstr -> list(tsubstr)
(lambda (lambda (regex_append $0 (regex_reverse_cdr (regex_split '.' $1)))))
description: A function that appends reversed substrings after splitting a full string by '.'

concat_with_w_prefix :: tsubstr -> tsubstr
(lambda (regex_concat 'w' $0))
description: A function that concatenates a given substring with a 'w' prefix.

append_list_of_substrings_to_given_string :: list(tsubstr) -> tsubstr -> tfullstr
(lambda (lambda (regex_flatten (regex_append $0 $1))))
description: A function that appends a list of substrings to a given string, flattening the list and appending each substring to the end of the given string.

split_string_into_list :: tfullstr -> list(tsubstr)
(lambda (regex_split empty_string $0))
description: A function that splits a full string into a list of substrings based on an empty string delimiter.

replace_substring_with_condition :: tsubstr -> tfullstr -> tfullstr
(lambda (lambda (replace_substring_based_on_condition $0 (lambda $2))))
description: A function that replaces substrings in a full string based on a condition provided by a transformation function.
Here are some example programs:
-- if there is i replace that with k t
(lambda (replace_if_match_split $0 (regex_concat 'k' 't') 'i'))
-- if there is p replace that with g
(lambda (replace_substrings_based_on_function $0 (lambda (regex_if (regex_match 'p' $0) 'g' $0))))
-- if the word ends with any letter add d after that
(lambda (append_list_of_substrings_to_given_string (split_string_into_list $0) 'd'))
-- if there is g replace that with u f
(lambda (replace_if_match_split $0 (regex_concat 'u' 'f') 'g'))
-- if the word starts with any letter replace that with b
(lambda (replace_first_letter_with_given_substring $0 'b'))
-- if there is t replace that with n
(lambda (replace_if_match_split $0 'n' 't'))
-- if there is any letter replace that with w t
(lambda (replace_substrings_based_on_function $0 (lambda (concat_with_w_prefix 't'))))
-- if the word starts with any letter replace that with w i
(lambda (replace_first_letter_with_given_substring $0 (concat_with_w_prefix 'i')))
-- if there is any letter add v after that
(lambda (replace_substrings_based_on_function $0 (lambda (regex_concat $0 'v'))))
-- if the word ends with consonant replace that with i
(lambda (regex_flatten (append_reversed_substrings_after_split $0 'i')))
-- if there is i replace that with m
(lambda (replace_substring_based_on_condition $0 (lambda (regex_if (regex_match $0 'i') 'm' $0))))
-- if there is vowel vowel replace that with y
